20th: The 3.7% lit #Moon sits above bright #Venus after sunset this evening. Look low to the west at around 19:00 UT. #Astronomy

19th: Bright Venus will be visible low to the west after sunset this evening. You can use it as a guide to find the very thin crescent #Moon. At only 0.6% illuminated and low down, it will be very tricky to find. #Astronomy
10th: Early this morning the 61% lit #Moon is close to Antares in Scorpius. Look low to the south-southeast from around 03:00 UT. #Astronomy

8th: Ganymede is occulted by Jupiter at 19:10 UT. It reappears at 22:29 UT before being eclipsed by Jupiter's shadow at 23:47 UT. #Astronomy

9th: Callisto is eclipsed by the shadow of #Jupiter at 20:16 UT this evening. It reappears at 00:32 UT tomorrow morning.

7th: There is a chance to spot Venus, Saturn and Neptune close together just after sunset this evening. They will be very low to the west around 19:00 UT. Neptune will be very difficult to spot due to the bright sky. Binoculars or a telescope best for this one. #Astronomy

1st: Jupiter's largest moon Ganymede will move into the planet's shadow at 19:48 UT. It reappears at 23:11 UT. An interesting sight through a telescope. #Astronomy
